question: Which of the following is the non-metallic form of mineral?
solution:
The correct answer is **"Mica".** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The inorganic materials that are found naturally as **minerals**. They can be found in a variety of settings. Crystalline structures and specific chemical compositions are characteristics of minerals.

 
• 
 
Metallic minerals are those that contain metals in their natural state.

 
 
• 
 
Examples of **metallic minerals** include bauxite, gold, silver, copper, and iron.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Minerals without any metal content are referred to as **non-metallic minerals.**

 
 
• 
 
When non-metallic minerals are liquefied, nothing new can be made from them, making them a unique class of chemical elements.

 
 
• 
 
Minerals like limestone, mica and gypsum, coal, and petroleum are examples of non-metallic minerals.

 
 
• 
 
Inorganic, non-metallic silicate makes up the majority of mica's chemical makeup.
